prompt_text: My air conditioning needs fixing in Phoenix. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
I can recommend companies — but to give the best, most specific options I need two quick details: which part of Phoenix (zip or neighborhood) and whether this is an emergency (no cool right now). If you want immediate calls, here’s a solid, practical plan (companies to contact + why), plus what to ask each when you call.

Who to call (good mix for fast service, authorized repairs, and competitive pricing)
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning / Benjamin Franklin franchises (Phoenix area)
  - Why: large local franchise network, typically available for fast same‑day or emergency service; standardized service procedures and written guarantees.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (Phoenix)
  - Why: large service organization with 24/7 emergency service, many technicians, and experience with a wide range of systems and refrigerants.
- Aire Serv (Phoenix)
  - Why: franchise network focused on HVAC with local technicians; they often have scheduled same‑day repairs and maintenance plans.
- Manufacturer-authorized dealer for your system brand (Carrier, Lennox, Trane, Bryant, etc.)
  - Why: if your system is still under warranty or if you want brand‑specific parts and certified techs, an authorized dealer is best. Use the manufacturer’s “Find a dealer” tool and pick a Phoenix dealer with high reviews.
- One well‑rated local independent HVAC contractor (search “HVAC Phoenix” + sort by Google/Yelp reviews and look for companies with many recent 4–5 star reviews)
  - Why: independents often give more competitive pricing and continuity with the same techs; they also know local load issues and permit requirements.

Why these choices
- National/franchise companies: speed, 24/7 emergency coverage, standard warranties and policies.
- Manufacturer dealers: brand knowledge and warranty protection, correct OEM parts.
- Local independents: often better price, personalized service, strong local reputation.

How to vet any company when you call
- Ask for their Arizona ROC (Registrar of Contractors) license number and verify it on the Arizona Registrar of Contractors site.
- Confirm they carry general liability insurance and worker’s comp.
- Ask whether technicians are NATE‑certified (industry standard).
- Ask about diagnostic fee, charge for trip/after‑hours, and whether the diagnostic fee is waived if you proceed with repairs.
- Ask what warranty they provide on parts and labor (get it in writing).
- Ask for a written estimate with itemized parts, labor, and permit costs if applicable.
- Ask if they use OEM parts or aftermarket, and if they can service your system brand.
- If your system uses R‑22 refrigerant, ask about availability and cost to recharge vs. cost of replacement (R‑22 is phased out and expensive).
- For emergency no‑cool situations: ask ETA and whether they have a truck stocked with common parts (capacitors, contactors, fan motors, refrigerant for your system).

How to choose among estimates
- Compare total price plus warranty length and what’s included (parts, labor, return visits).
- Prefer companies that provide a clear written scope (repair vs. replace), energy‑efficiency advice, and disclose any upcharges for after‑hours or weekends.
- If a company gives a dramatically low quote, confirm they are licensed and insured—low price can mean cut corners.

If this is urgent (no cooling right now, high risk for infants/elderly/pets)
- Call the largest local franchise (One Hour or ARS) for fastest ETA.
- If you have a manufacturer warranty, call the brand dealer first.
- Ask each company for an ETA, whether they’ll arrive with replacement parts, and if they can temporarily restore cooling while waiting for parts.

If you want, tell me:
- Your neighborhood/zip code and system brand/model or age and the symptom (no cool, short‑cycling, leaking, weird noises). I’ll return a short list of 3–5 specific Phoenix companies (with phone and one‑line reason to call each) tailored to your location and system.
